Q3051496.label: 1935 Polish legislative election
Q3051496.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 8 September 1935, with Senate elections held a week later on 15 September. They were held under the April Constitution, drawn up earlier in 1935 by the Sanation movement, which had changed the electoral system to one more in its favor. In protest, the opposition boycotted the elections and voter turnout was only 45.9%, the lowest in the history of the Second Republic.

Q828392.label: People's Party – Movement for a Democratic Slovakia
Q828392.wiki: People's Party – Movement for a Democratic Slovakia
Q828392.summary: The People's Party – Movement for a Democratic Slovakia, known as the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia until 2003, was a conservative and populist political party in Slovakia. It was founded in 1991 following a split from Public Against Violence and dissolved in 2014. Throughout its existence, the party was led by its founder, Vladimír Mečiar. HZDS was considered a personalistic party built around Mečiar's cult of the leader. At the same time, it was a mass party with over 70,000 members at its peak.

Q37860840.label: Robert Abela
Q37860840.summary: Robert Abela is a Maltese lawyer and politician who has served as prime minister of Malta and leader of the Malta Labour Party since 2020, following the resignation of Joseph Muscat on 13 January that year. The son of former president George Abela, he was elected to Parliament in 2017.

Q254440.label: 1999 Estonian parliamentary election
Q254440.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Estonia on 7 March 1999. The newly elected 101 members of the 9th Riigikogu assembled at Toompea Castle in Tallinn within ten days of the election. The elections proved disastrous for the ruling Estonian Coalition Party, which won only seven seats together with two of its smaller allies.

Q13424616.label: 1926 Lithuanian parliamentary election
Q13424616.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Lithuania between 8 and 10 May 1926. The Lithuanian Popular Peasants' Union remained the largest party, winning 24 of the 85 seats in the third Seimas. They formed a left-wing coalition government with the Social Democratic Party of Lithuania, which was overthrown in a military coup in December. The Seimas was disbanded in 1927 and Lithuanian Nationalist Union leader Antanas Smetona was appointed President.

Q4247016.label: Kumul Rebellion
Q4247016.summary: The Kumul Rebellion was a rebellion from 1931 to 1934 of Kumulik Uyghurs who conspired with Hui Chinese Muslim General Ma Zhongying to overthrow Jin Shuren, the governor of Xinjiang Province. The Kumulik Uyghurs were loyal to the Kumul Khanate and wanted to restore the heir to the khanate and overthrow Jin. The Kuomintang wanted Jin removed because of his unapproved negotiations with the Soviet Union, so Chinese Premier Chiang Kai-shek secretly approved of the operation while ostensibly acknowledging Jin as governor.

Q8680.label: British Empire
Q8680.desc: overseas possessions of England and later the United Kingdom (1607–1997)
Q8680.summary: The British Empire comprised the dominions, colonies, protectorates, mandates, and other territories ruled or administered by the United Kingdom and its predecessor states. It began with the overseas possessions and trading posts established by England in the late 16th and early 17th centuries, and colonisation attempts by Scotland during the 17th century. At its height in the 19th and early 20th centuries, it was the largest empire in history and, for a century, was the foremost global power.

Country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

Q3048.label: Charles Maurras
Q3048.desc: French author, politician, poet, and critic (1868–1952)
Q3048.summary: Charles-Marie-Photius Maurras was a French author, politician, poet and critic. He was an organiser and principal philosopher of Action Française, a political movement that was monarchist, medievalist, conservative, corporatist, integralist, nationalist and counter-revolutionary. Maurras was staunchly against capitalism, communism, Freemasonry, liberalism, Islam, Jews, Nazism and Protestantism. His ideas greatly influenced National Catholicism and integral nationalism, and led to the political doctrine of Maurrassisme.

Influenced by: François-René de La Tour du Pin, Chambly de La Charce

Q1000.label: Gabon
Q1000.desc: country on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa
Q1000.summary: Gabon, officially the Gabonese Republic, is a country on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, lying on the equator. It is bordered by Equatorial Guinea to the northwest, Cameroon to the north, the Republic of the Congo to the east and south, while sharing a maritime border with São Tomé and Príncipe to the west in the Gulf of Guinea. It has an area of 270,000 square kilometres (100,000 sq mi) and a population of 2.6 million people. There are coastal plains, mountains, and savanna in the east. Libreville is the capital and largest city; other major cities include Port-Gentil and Franceville.
